- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.3) and forecast remains elevated, lower the forecast by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- Avoid forecasting a 30-day trend that diverges from recent 7–14 day mean; use rolling average as a sanity check.  
- Overshoots after spikes (especially >10% above recent high) are common; cap forecast at +5% above 14-day moving average.  
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings) and forecast is smooth, introduce a 1–2 day lag in the forecast’s peak to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), adjust forecast to reflect downward slope starting at day +3.
